title: Forestry
text:
CFFDRS-2.0: Wildfire Risk Mapping


Operational workflow for wildfire risk mapping and fuel typing in accordance with the updated Canadian Forest Fire Danger Rating System (V2.0) for British Columbia’s Okanagan Watershed. This reproducible workflow integrates satellite-derived elevation data, gridded climate variables from Environment and Climate Change Canada weather stations, and BC Vegetation Resource Inventory (VRI) datasets. The methodology processes Digital Elevation Models, applies Inverse Distance Weighting interpolation for climate data, and implements Wotton and Beverly’s stand-adjusted fine-fuel moisture content model. Using the cffdrs R package, the workflow generates Fire Weather Index (FWI), Initial Spread Index (ISI), and Build-up Index (BUI) raster outputs. Features comprehensive fuel type classification based on species composition and stand density, producing Head Fire Index and Fire Intensity predictions to support operational fire management teams, researchers, and wildfire risk assessment applications.





Feb 24, 2022












LiDAR: Ash Dieback Stem Mapping


LiDAR workflow for mapping ash dieback disease (Hymenoscyphus fraxineus) using high-resolution point cloud data and field validation. Combines canopy metrics with ground data to detect disease progression patterns, quantify canopy gaps from ash mortality, and map stem distribution changes over time. Features automated algorithms for identifying healthy versus declining ash trees through LiDAR-derived crown metrics, supporting targeted forest health interventions and silvicultural planning in diseased stands.





Mar 12, 2022












LiDAR: Forest Height Analysis


Stand height analysis combining LiDAR and photogrammetric data for operational forest inventory planning. Features automated tree top detection algorithms, canopy height model generation, and stand structure characterization supporting efficient field plot allocation and sampling design. Includes crown delineation protocols, diameter-height relationship modeling, and accessibility analysis for optimizing field crew deployment in complex terrain environments.

LiDAR: Forestry Guidebook


End-to-end workflow for processing raw airborne LiDAR point cloud data into digital terrain models and normalized canopy height products. Includes individual tree detection and crown segmentation methodologies, stems-per-hectare estimation using both point-based and raster-based approaches, and LAScatalog batch processing techniques for memory-efficient handling of large-scale datasets.

Allometry Validation


Instructor


Statistical validation and calibration procedures for allometric biomass models compliant with ART-TREES requirements for carbon registry emissions reporting. Technical guidance in model selection methodology is specifically aimed at avoiding Types 1-4 statistical errors and over-fitting. Carbon registries mandate robust model selection protocols to monitor predictive accuracy for signs of systematic bias and apply correction through hyper parameter tuning.


Aug 2024






Integrated Mapping of Wetland Dynamics in an Endorheic Lake Basin: Weaving Remote Sensing & Community Mapping Methods Together


Instructor


Methodological workshop on integrating satellite remote sensing with participatory community mapping to monitor wetland dynamics and fishing activity in Lake Chilwa Basin, Malawi. The workflow combines a longitudinal Landsat time series (1994-2015), Sentinel-1 InSAR data, and extensive mixed-methods fieldwork to examine enforcement conflicts and management opportunities in Africa’s most densely populated wetland ecosystem.


Jan 2020

title: Mapping
text:
Interactive mapping templates and cartographic workflows for geospatial analysis and visualization. View the complete collection at my map templates website.

















Site Maps:


Collection of site maps, including static maps designed for field operations teams and interactive maps for collective review of waypoints or target locations. Static maps were derived to ensure customizable basemaps, project boundary delineation, geographic coordinate grid and graticule cross-hairs. Legends were added using tmap functions that ensure minimum cartographic features are rendered including scale bars and north arrows.





Dec 15, 2024












Population Maps:


Robust template and data source for rapid population density and demographic analysis useful for community impact assessments and initial stakeholder mapping. Visualizing census data and human settlements, population maps provide key tools at initial stages or during ex-post project evaluations.





Nov 20, 2024












Watershed Maps:


Three-dimensional topographic delineation of the surrounding immediate watershed sub-basin. Watershed mapping provides essential resources for hydrological analysis of catchment dynamics, shared boundary, and flow direction analysis. This workflow includes tools for drainage area calculations, outlet point identification, stream network and contour visualizations, which are used to inform environmental impact studies and risk assessment between upstream and downstream features.





Nov 28, 2024












Riparian Maps:


Riparian map including DEM conditioning by breaching and filling depressions and flats, and stream delineation using flow direction and accumulation rendered in 3D over elevation data designed to support wetland conservation, streambank stabilization projects, and riparian vegetation management strategies.





Sep 20, 2025












Climate Maps:


Climate maps featuring mean daily temperature (°C), precipitation (mm³/day), relative humidity (%), and wind speed (m/s) derived from Environment and Climate Change Canada weather station data using Inverse Distance Weighting interpolation. Station data aggregated over specified periods and spatially interpolated to continuous raster surfaces, supporting wildfire risk assessment, agricultural planning, environmental monitoring, and climate impact studies for operational decision-making.





Aug 1, 2025












Topography Maps:


Topographic maps featuring classified slope percentages and cardinal aspects derived from conditioned DEM data. These maps support terrain assessment, erosion risk evaluation, slope stability analysis, and site suitability planning for infrastructure development, agricultural practices, and environmental management operations.





Aug 1, 2025












Mapping Templates: Site Visualization


Collection of every-day maps used operational site mapping designed to support fieldwork and environmental analysis activities. This resource includes topographic, hydrographic, demographic, and watershed cartographic tools. Site maps were designed for supporting boundary identification and field access, with Locator inset maps also provided for helping users within quickly orientate themselves within local and national landscapes. A final section was added showcasing 3-D mapping of watershed delineation and topopgrahy useful for environmental impact assessments between upstream and downstream sites. These templates serve as practical tools for researchers, environmental analysts, and field professionals requiring standardized every-day mapping solutions for site orientation and operational planning.





Dec 4, 2024












Wetlands Mapping: SAR & Landsat Workflows


Framework for mapping endorheic wetland dynamics, combining Sentinel-1 InSAR processing with Landsat time series analysis (1994-2015), using water extraction indices (NDWI, MNDWI, AWEIsh) and spectral mixture analysis for sub-pixel water detection. Community mapping components include key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and rapid participatory appraisals capturing local ecological knowledge of seasonal fishing migration patterns and traditional resource management practices.





Jun 15, 2024

Open-source mobile data collection framework built on Open Data Kit (GeoODK) architecture for socioeconomic field surveys. Provides customizable survey templates, GPS-enabled data collection forms, with automated quality control protocols, multilingual support, and integrated statistical sampling tools using android mobile devices

title: Seamus Murphy
text:
GitHub

My name is Seamus Murphy and I’m a forester specializing in stand mensuration and carbon verification. I completed my PhD at SOAS, University of London in 2015 and an MSc in Environmental Forestry at Bangor University in 2019. As a Registered Professional Forester (SIFTM #1125) and Forest Carbon Analyst at TÜV SÜD, I audit carbon offset programs under VCS, ACR, ARB, PEFC, and ART standards.
Over the years, I have observed forest monitoring systems fail not from flawed science, but from inaccessible workflows and poor documentation. This drives my commitment to developing open-source tools and reproducible frameworks in R and Python that verification teams can deploy and maintain. From Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification to enhanced forest inventory protocols, I prioritize transparent methods, QA/QC documentation, and version-controlled workflows (2026, 2025a, 2025b, 2025c, 2022c).
Workflows also cover applications in LiDAR, RADAR, and multispectral imagery for forest health monitoring (2023a, 2024a), as well as in-situ data scaling, GPS accuracy assessments and open-source survey deployment systems (2019, 2021a, 2021b, 2022a, 2022b).
